question: Which of the following dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate finally annexed Jaunpur into the empire of Delhi Sultanate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lodi dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Lodi dynasty**, under Sikandar Lodi, annexed Jaunpur into the Delhi Sultanate in 1494.
 
• Jaunpur had been an independent sultanate established after the disintegration of the Tughlaq dynasty but was brought back under Delhi's control during Sikandar Lodi’s reign.
 
• Sikandar Lodi pursued aggressive expansion policies and sought to consolidate territories lost during earlier dynasties.
 
• The annexation of Jaunpur strengthened the Lodi dynasty’s influence in northern India and ensured the unification of key territories under the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Jaunpur became an important administrative and cultural center under Sikandar Lodi after its reintegration into the Delhi Sultanate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lodi Dynasty Overview:**

 
 
• The Lodi dynasty (1451–1526) was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate and was founded by Bahlul Lodi.
 
• Sikandar Lodi (r. 1489–1517) was one of the most prominent rulers of the dynasty, known for his administrative reforms and military campaigns.
 
 
 
• **Jaunpur Sultanate:**
 
 
• The Jaunpur Sultanate was established by Malik Sarwar, a former governor of the Tughlaq dynasty, in 1394.
 
• It flourished as a center of learning and culture, earning the nickname "Shiraz of India" during its independence.
 
 
 
• **Sikandar Lodi’s Achievements:**
 
 
• He reorganized tax administration and promoted agriculture to strengthen the economy.
 
• He was a patron of Persian culture and literature, further enriching the intellectual landscape of his era.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate:**
 
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was a Muslim kingdom based in Delhi that ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent from 1206 to 1526.
 
• It saw five major dynasties: the Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi dynasties.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Lodi Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Lodi dynasty ended in 1526 when Ibrahim Lodi was defeated by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat, leading to the establishment of the Mughal Empire.
